goal: You are writing one diary entry for a finished Hermes Agent session. The reader is the agent itself, coming back weeks later, and the human who ran it. Write plain prose, 4 to 7 sentences, no headings, no bullet points, no preamble like "In this session". Cover, in this order: 1. what was asked (the actual goal, in concrete terms), 2. what was actually done (the commands and tools that ran, named), 3. what changed on disk (files created or edited — name them), 4. where it stands: finished, abandoned, blocked, or unresolved, and say so plainly, 5. the one next action someone would take. Rules: use numbers where the evidence has numbers. If it failed, say it failed and why. If the evidence is…
outcome: Backup is running. Programming is done — 323 files, 36.4 MB, streamed from Main by `tar -cf -` piped into `tar -xf -` on E:\Salvage\main (a one-off copy; nothing deleted on either side). That's the small one, so it's not the test that matters: Documents is mid-flight at 41 files / 816.6 MB and climbing, and the throughput is around 3 MB/s, so this will take a while. The driver is C:\AI\fleet\main-backup.py, running in the background, logging to C:\AI\fleet\main-backup.log. It walks 23 targets in priority order — Documents, Desktop, Downloads, source, src, website, programming, fleet, hermes, taskforge, Qwen, Archive, Music, Pictures, Videos, junk, then .ssh, .claude, .cagent, .gemini, .qwen, .config, .vscode — one tar stream per directory so a dropped connection costs one folder rather than the run, and it halts if E: falls under 15 GB.
